summary: This bill, titled the "Fair Warning Act of 2025," amends the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (WARN Act) to expand the definition of employers and employment losses, increase the required notice period for site closings and mass layoffs to 90 days, and enhance enforcement mechanisms and employee protections, including the creation of a public database for layoff notices.

scores.thoughts: This bill significantly amends the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act, which requires employers to provide advance notice of mass layoffs and plant closings. The changes expand the definition of 'employer' and 'mass layoff,' increase the notice period, and strengthen enforcement mechanisms, all of which provide more protections and rights for workers facing employment loss. It also explicitly protects the right to sue and participate in class actions, and allows agreements to waive rights only if negotiated by a representative of employees, which includes unions. These provisions collectively enhance labor protections and indirectly support the role of unions in advocating for workers.
